CHIEF COMPLAINT
Low back pain with right foot paresthesias.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who presents with acute onset low back pain that began yesterday while raking leaves in his yard. Approximately two hours after completing yard work, he developed tightening of the low back and pins and needles sensation in his right foot. Patient reports this is his first significant episode in three years. He has tried ice and ibuprofen 200 mg (two tablets) without relief. Pain is partially alleviated with heat (hot shower) and sitting. Pain worsens with forward flexion and improves with standing up from flexed position. Denies significant physical activity prior to this incident.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for right lower extremity paresthesias. Negative for bowel or bladder dysfunction.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Low back pain approximately three years ago, self-limited, resolved after one day.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen (over-the-counter, two tablets attempted).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Sedentary lifestyle. Rarely engages in physical activity. Lives with partner.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Not documented.
Low back: Pain with forward flexion. No pain with extension. Tenderness to palpation at L5 level. Neurological exam: Dorsiflexion intact bilaterally. Pulses equal in all extremities. Paresthesias noted in right lower extremity.

RESULTS
X-ray of low back: Normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute low back strain secondary to yard work activity.
2. Right lower extremity paresthesias, likely radicular in nature.
Plan: Rest and activity modification. Start meloxicam for pain management. Referral to physical therapy for strengthening and stretching exercises. Follow-up in two weeks. Will consider MRI if symptoms do not improve within two weeks. Patient to contact office with any worsening symptoms.
